purpose: Conditional structural bounds for CQ3 (and directional context for CQ4) only.
adapter_disclosures: IDENTIFIED (growth only): the model is PPP-based (demand.ts: "PPP, 2017 international dollars", world ~$158T). Its deflator base year is 2017, not the brief's constant-2025-USD-PPP lock. CQ3 asks for a GROWTH RATE, which is invariant to the deflator base, so the translation is identified. A LEVEL question would NOT be.

COVERAGE GAP: "OECD-38 + China" is proxied by us + oecd-ex-us + china. The model's nine regions place Korea, Japan and Turkiye in seasia/mena and Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica in latam, so several real OECD-38 members sit outside the proxy and some non-OECD states sit inside oecd-ex-us. Treat the growth figure as an OECD-core + China aggregate, not as the OECD-38 + China aggregate.

PRIOR CONFLICT: CLAUDE.md records that the model's demographic path tracks the UN WPP LOW variant (~18% below the medium variant by 2100) by deliberate low-fertility-convergence choice. That biases the model's labour force, and therefore its growth, DOWNWARD relative to the brief's locked Section 2A baseline. Any CQ3 bound read off this model is a LOW-FERTILITY-CONDITIONAL bound.

NOT IDENTIFIED (CQ4): capital.interestRate is an economy-wide REAL interest rate. The model has no 10-year sovereign benchmark, no term premium (no termPremium anywhere in src/), and no inflation swap or breakeven. It therefore CANNOT produce the G7 GDP-weighted 10y sovereign real yield CQ4 asks for. The rate and debtRiskPremium below are reported as DIRECTIONAL context only and must not be used as a CQ4 point estimate.

NOT REPRESENTABLE (CQ1, CQ2, CQ5): src/modules/ contains no unemployment, no ISIC sector split, no sectoral median wage, no price level, no CPI/PCE, no asset prices and no volatility index. The model is entirely real. Do not derive any CQ1, CQ2 or CQ5 number from it.

PARTIAL (CQ6): only the GROWTH leg of the regime definitions is modellable via CQ3. The >=2.7% and <2.0% core-inflation conditions are not representable, so the model can discriminate A-vs-not-A on growth and speak to D's growth leg, but cannot place mass between C and D.

GLOBAL vs REGIONAL: dataCenterLoadTWh and robotsPer1000 are WORLD aggregates in this model, while the brief's AI-Q3 prior is an OECD-38 + China figure. The model number is therefore an UPPER bound on the AI-Q3 quantity, not a like-for-like comparison.

refusals.CQ1: not representable - no unemployment, no ISIC sectors, no sectoral median wage
refusals.CQ2: not representable - the model has no price level
refusals.CQ4: not identified - economy-wide real rate is not a 10y sovereign real yield; no term premium
refusals.CQ5: not representable - no asset prices, no volatility index
